amy: Quick check-in — turned on the interleaved-queue credit rebalancer on staging at 09:10 UTC. Observed immediate drop in short-request p50 but p99 for long requests spiked ~120ms. wondering if kv-cache churn or kernel mismatch. :thinking:
ben: saw same in the trace dashboard, p99 jump coincides with more kernel-switches logged by perf-bot around 09:10. attaching short excerpt from logs below.
chris: can you paste the kernel selection lines? i'm curious if the selector picked fast-fp16 kernel or fell back to slower int8 path.
ben: logs: `2026-03-18T09:10:12Z perf-bot kernel_select tenant=t3 model=llama-70b variant=quant8 reason=kv-warmup-fallback selected_kernel=int8_v2`
amy: exact. the rebalancer is aggressively reallocating token credits from long lanes to short lanes every 250ms; when long lanes drop below threshold it triggers kv-evict to free slots and we hit a lot of kernel fallback churn.
jordan: hypothesis: short requests get fast path but steal KV cache entries, causing long sequences to miss and go through a cold KV path -> kernel change -> higher latency. Could add a soft reserve for long lanes.
chris: proposal: soft_reserve_tokens = max(64, 0.15 * tenant_token_target) applied per tenant long-lane. Also change rebalancer to prefer credit loans with a 500ms min hold to avoid immediate churn.
amy: +1. added a trial config on staging: `soft_reserve_tokens: 128, loan_hold_ms: 500, evict_threshold: 0.8`
perf-bot: profiling snapshot @09:12:20
```
GPU kernels: fast_fp16 67% tokens serviced
              int8_v2   28% tokens serviced
              slow_cpu 5% tokens serviced
KV hit rate: long-lane 62% -> 48% (pre->post)
             short-lane 74% -> 81%
p99 latency long-lane: 420ms -> 540ms
p50 latency short-lane: 38ms -> 28ms
```
ben: that kv hit delta on long-lane is concerning. We might be thrashing a small shared cache due to tenant eviction scoring.
chris: what's the eviction scoring algorithm right now? LRU + tenant_weight?
amy: current score = recency_factor * LRU_age + tenant_weight * (1 / active_streams). It biases towards evicting entries from tenants with more active short streams.
jordan: idea: add sequence_length_factor to score so very long sequences are penalized less (i.e., protected). score = base_score - alpha * min(seq_len, 1024). alpha tuned per model.
ben: that would raise the cost to evict entries used by long sequences. also consider a separate per-tenant KV partition quota: reserve N slots for pinned sequences.
chris: downside: reduces overall cache util. need to simulate hit rate vs memory footprint. I ran a micro-sim yesterday: protecting 10% of slots for long sequences kept long-lane hit rate stable but short-lane dropped ~3%, overall tokens/sec unchanged.
amy: acceptable tradeoff if p99 stabilizes. Let's roll the soft_reserve + eviction scoring change to canary and measure p99 over 30m. Also add rebalancer cooldown increase to 750ms if churn detected.
perf-bot: canary started 09:25 UTC, canary_id=cbr-42
ben: quick command I used for telemetry queries: `telemetry query --from 09:00 --to 09:40 "model=llama-70b and tenant=~t3.*" --metrics p50,p95,p99,kv_hit_rate,kernel_switches`
chris: also add a gauge for 'loan_count' and 'loan_retention_ms' so we can see whether loans are sticky or flip-flopping.
jordan: if we still see p99 regressions, fallback is to prefer kernel affinity over immediate latency: i.e., when kernel_select would change kernel we instead enqueue to a kernel-bound batch (slower immediate throughput but preserves KV locality).
amy: noted. timeline: canary runs 30m, if p99_long < +10% of baseline and overall throughput within -5% we push to staging-wide. otherwise revert. I'll post results at 09:55. :hourglass: 
ben: thanks — i'll watch traces for kernel_switch spikes and tag them. :eyes: 
chris: adding a short alert: if kernel_switches per 1m > 200 and p99_long > baseline*1.15 then page `eng-runtime-oncall`.
amy: perfect. updating PR with config toggles and telemetry. will link once ready.
perf-bot: perf snapshot @09:55:30 after soft_reserve+scoring
```
KV hit rate: long-lane 63% -> 61% (pre->post-candidate)
             short-lane 74% -> 78%
kernel_switches/min: 310 -> 92
p99 long-lane: 540ms -> 448ms
p50 short-lane: 28ms -> 30ms
```
amy: initial looks promising — kernel switches down, long p99 improving but still slightly above baseline. keeping canary running 30m more.
jordan: good work. follow-up action: we should add a unit test for eviction scoring and a simulation harness for rebalancer loan dynamics.
amy: added to backlog ticket RT-998. will assign and follow up. :white_check_mark:
